sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x bibliography for yate1242 (langdoc query, 6 refs) and ISO 639-3 Change Request 2006-027 record
sources.note: Only Jaeger & Van Valin 1982 (phonology) and Van Valin 1998 (specific feature) are descriptive; others are ethnographic/overview (González Rojas 2016; Bauer-Thoma 1916; Urcid 2005). ISO record documents the 2007 merge of [ztc] Lachirioag into [zty].

sources.citation: Lingmex: Bibliografía Lingüística de México desde 1970 (El Colegio de México), search 'Yateé'/'Yatee'/'Lachirioag' via /Public/BusquedaSimple API, 2026-09-17
sources.note: Three records only: Jaeger & Van Valin 1982 (Fonética y Fonología), Van Valin 1998 (Morfosintaxis), Vázquez Vázquez & Romero Frizzi 2011 Tlalocan 17 (colonial título primordial of San Francisco Yatee). No thesis or grammar on Yateé/Lachirioag Zapotec; 'Lachirioag' returns zero.

sources.citation: LAPSyD (Lyon-Albuquerque Phonological Systems Database) ISO index; WALS language list; SIL-Mexico language pages (checked 2026-09-17)
sources.note: No Yatee/Yateé Zapotec entry in LAPSyD or WALS; SIL Mexico has no zty page (no ILV work on this variety). AILLA lists 36 audio files (15 h) for zty but no written description.

sources.citation: Van Valin, Robert D. Jr. Curriculum vitae (archived copy, web.archive.org 2022-05-17 of acsu.buffalo.edu/~vanvalin/)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Confirms the only Yateé publications are Jaeger & Van Valin 1982 and Van Valin 1998; no unpublished Yateé phonology listed.

sources.citation: Arellanes Arellanes, Francisco. 2009. El sistema fonológico y las propiedades fonéticas del zapoteco de San Pablo Güilá: descripción y análisis formal. Tesis doctoral, El Colegio de México.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Cites Jaeger & Van Valin 1982 (p.125, 127: 'All Zapotecan languages are tone languages') and Jaeger 1983: 180 on voicing of Yaté lenis obstruents; nothing about Yateé stress.

sources.citation: Yasugi, Yoshiho. 1995. Native Middle American Languages: An Areal-Typological Perspective (Senri Ethnological Studies 39). Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Appendix entry 'Yatee [JAEGER and VAN VALIN 1982] (19C+ʔ, 4V)' on p.202 lists fortis/lenis consonants, vowels i e a o (plain and checked), 'Tones: high, low, low-to-high rising, high-to-low falling', loan phonemes; no stress/accent line for Yatee (other entries in the same appendix do carry 'Stress is phonemic' / 'Accent falls on the penultimate' lines when the source gives one). Tone survey p.55 lists 'Zapotec (Yatee, Juarez: rising, falling)' under three tones plus combinations. Second-hand and silent on stress.
